plate_findings.evidence: Caption: "centripetal hyperfluorescence of the edges of the active lesion"; the sequence shows late hyperfluorescent leakage at the lesion margins.
Caption: "hyper-reflectivity and thickening of the inner layers of the retina."

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Fundus photograph from an article specifically on ocular toxoplasmosis showing the captioned active juxta-papillary retinochoroiditis lesion. [raw subtype: active retinochoroiditis (Jensen)] B: Angiographic sequence demonstrates hyperfluorescence progressing from the active retinochoroiditis lesion margins with associated late serous retinal detachment, supporting ocular toxoplasmosis. [raw subtype: active retinochoroiditis (Jensen)] C: OCT shows acute retinal hyperreflectivity and thickening, with vitreous hyperreflective points and serous retinal detachment, consistent with active ocular toxoplasmosis. [raw subtype: active retinochoroiditis (Jensen)]

panels.figure_caption: (A) Fundus Photo: Juxta papillary active retinochoroiditis (Jensen). (B) Angiographic sequence of Jensen's retinochoroiditis: centripetal hyperfluorescence of the edges of the active lesion. To note that the serous retinal detachment is best seen in the late phase. (C) OCT: hyper-reflectivity and thickening of the inner layers of the retina, hyper-reflective vitreous points, and serous retinal detachment.
in_text_mentions: Seven active lesions and five retinochoroidal scars were studied. In the acute phase (Fig. 1), thickening, hyper-reflectivity of the neurosensory retina, posterior shading and bumping of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) were found. The choroid became thickened and hyporeflective (Table 1). The choroidal hyporeflectivity may be partially related to the hyperreflectivity of the retinal deeper layers.
